run: the user's rmc-fit-assessment interview, 2026-10-24 (the code half: the convergence rule, the constraint-limited rule and two checks on the answer); implemented and checked on the Demo and the dev cases: arms A, A+ and D on the dev set before (8edf8c0) and after (0fe4bdf), the model-visible snapshots, the answer corpus and the scripted replays, 2026-10-24
evidence: The user's answers in the rmc-fit-assessment interview, 2026-10-24. (1) Convergence on every fit term and the total: until now the chi^2 history the Copilot and the watchdog judged was the last .log column only (the Demo's X_ray_(R)1; dev-fit-unconverged's too), and 'improving' meant a windowDelta beyond a fixed 0.02 in ln chi^2 over the last 20 %, which no noise entered: a slow decline of 0.4 % per tenth read 'converged' or 'stalled', a noisy flat history could read 'improving'. The user's rule: a run is converged only when no term and not the total is still falling beyond its noise over the last tenth of the run. Taken as: a least-squares line through each series' last tenth (at least 10 rows, never back past the last restart, since a restart recomputes chi^2) falls when its fitted change exceeds k = 3 times the residual sd about it. k = 3 is the app's 3-sigma bar: for a flat series of independent noise the fitted change across m rows has sd sigma*sqrt(12(m-1)/(m(m+1))), at most 0.99 sigma from m = 10 on and 0.23 sigma over the Demo's 227-row window, so a flat series passes for falling with probability 0.8 % at 10 rows (Student's t, 8 df; 0.9 % simulated) and never in 2000 simulated 227-row windows; noise correlated from row to row (lag-1 0.9) gives 0.25 % over 227 rows and 8.6 % over 50, where the rule errs towards 'still moving', never towards 'converged'. The change is compared with the scatter, not a t statistic that grows with the row count. Known answers (heuristics.test.js): a flat noisy history after a drop is converged; ln chi^2 = 1 + 0.3 exp(-t/1000) with noise 0.001 falls by about 0.006 over its last tenth, about 6 times its noise, so it is improving where the old rule read it flat; one term decaying while a dominant flat term holds the total flat is improving (the charted column alone read converged); a jump at a restart inside the last tenth is no trend. The Demo (2262 rows, three logs): F(Q)_1 falls by 0.016 (noise 0.0015) and X_ray_(R)1 by 0.12 (noise 0.0027); the two curvature constraints in use are flat (0.073 against 0.025, 0.098 against 0.05); four curvature columns are zero throughout; their total falls by 0.074 against 0.024 (3.03 times); status improving, as before. dev-fit-unconverged: both terms and the total fall by 0.031-0.035, 14 to 23 times their noise; improving, as its truth says. (2) The constraint-limited rule: 'g(r) above 5 % of the peak at the cut means the peak is constraint-limited; interpret nothing on its low-r side, and suggest rerunning with the constraint loosened.' Until now the pile-up test shared the shell separation's 2 %. On the Demo no reading moves: Ga-Se 8.7 % at its 2.2 A constraint is limited under both, Ta-Se 1.4 % under neither, the other pairs 0; no dev case has a .dat, so no constraint. (3) Two firm rules on the answer: order claimed at a box-scale wavevector (a long wave, every |q_i| <= 0.25, the modulation engine's isLongWave: 'a long wave is a correlation the finite box can't represent, so it says nothing about order at its own q; a point or mode that passes its own test at another q is judged on that test alone'), and a distribution quoted from a single configuration without saying so (the app always analyses one configuration). On the answer corpus (ten real answers) the checks raise one new finding and no false alarm: the README GIF's GaSe4 answer quotes the Se-Ga-Se angle distribution and the Ga coordination counts without saying they come from one configuration (judged right). (4) The user's answers 2, 5 and 6 as scripted replays on the Demo where a check can catch the wrong answer: answer 2 (a first-shell number with a 'still improving' caveat passes, 'converged' is flagged), answer 5 (the angle distribution said to come from the one configuration of a run with 3.52 accepted moves per atom passes, the bare form is flagged), answer 6 (Se's strongest mode, a long wave at q = (0.1, 0.2, -0.1), called order is flagged). No check can catch, and no rule was added for: an Rw below the data's noise taken for a better fit, a detailed claim about a partial under 5 % of the signal, a feature that differs between independent runs, whether a subtle effect waits for the run to finish, the 10 accepted moves per atom past convergence, and a small effect quoted from one configuration. Arms A, A+ and D on the dev set before (8edf8c0) and after (0fe4bdf): all 45 records identical, so validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json is not re-recorded. Approved by the user, 2026-10-24.
proposed_fix: Implemented as the user answered. Parsing (both runtimes): readChi / read_chi_log read every chi^2 column after Time, moves_acc and moves_gen (CHI_TERMS_START), each row's total and the rows per log; plotData.chiTerms = {names, series, total, segments} in the chart's ln transform (browserData.js chiTermsPlotData, combineChiTerms; plots.chi_terms_payload through /api/plot/data; plotDataCache.js turns its nulls into NaN); the per-term histories concatenate only when every log names the same terms; the chart still draws the last column. The rule (src/llm/watchdog/heuristics.js): seriesTrend (TREND_WINDOW_FRACTION 0.1, TREND_MIN_ROWS 10, TREND_NOISE_FACTOR 3, never back past the last restart), judgeConvergence over every term and the total (diverging on a non-finite latest value or a rising total; improving when any series falls; diverging when a term rises and none falls; stalled when flat and none ever dropped by MIN_TOTAL_DROP; terms zero throughout listed apart), classifyConvergence kept for one series. assess_convergence (its description, and its result: window_rows, total, terms, zero_terms, chart_column in place of column, first/last/min, total_drop and slope_per_step), the context's convergence section (last_10pct with each term's and the total's change, noise_sd and trend, in place of change_over_last_10pct and recent_slope_per_step; CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET 6000 -> 6500 characters, so the Demo's second g(r) peaks stay), the system prompt's watchdog_status sentence, the answer check's finding and the watchdog badge (useWatchdog, its narration and its title; AGENTS.md's next step 6 asked for the badge on the total) read the one verdict. The constraint: shells.js CONSTRAINT_LIMIT_FRACTION = 0.05, SEPARATION_G_FRACTION 0.02 for the shell separation only; find_gr_peaks' warning 'constraint-limited: interpret nothing on its low-r side; consider rerunning with the constraint loosened', the advice as method (arm C reads the reading alone). The checks (src/llm/copilot/verification/facts.js): long-wave in the modulation row (analyze_modulations' facts.modulation gains long_wave_q and long_waves; a clause that claims order at a q whose every |q_i| is within the bound, or at a long or box-scale wave in words, is flagged; a clause that denies order claims none) and single-configuration, a new distribution row (compute_bond_angles, analyze_displacement_directions and analyze_clusters return facts.distribution with configurations 1; an answer quoting a distribution's numbers without saying one configuration is flagged). Model-visible: the system prompt +226 characters in every variant; assess_convergence's description 274 -> 575 characters and its Demo result 435 -> 1111; read_run_data's description +58 and its convergence section 706 -> 1093; the Demo context +486 characters (the dock's worst turn +429 tokens, arm B's on dev-fit-unconverged +359; contextBudget.test.js pins).
